contents.text: An HG-400 gearbox has this problem: oil leaks at a shaft. What could cause it?
Oil leaks at a shaft may be caused by a worn shaft seal or a blocked breather. Oil leaks at a shaft may also be caused by a problem with the cooling fins.

HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 5 Operation › 5.2 Operating limits
## 5.2 Operating limits
Stop the gearbox and find the cause if the oil temperature exceeds 90 °C, if the noise changes suddenly or if oil leaks from a shaft seal.
A whining noise that rises with speed usually points to a low oil level or worn gear teeth.
# 6 Maintenance
Table 6-1 Maintenance schedule
| Task | Interval |
|---|---|
| Check the oil level at the sight glass | Weekly |
| Check for leaks and unusual noise | Weekly |
| Oil analysis for viscosity, water and metal particles | Every 6 months |
| Change the oil | As Table 4-1 |
| Replace the shaft seals | Every 20,000 h or when leaking |

HG-400 Helical Gearbox Operating Manual › 7 Troubleshooting
# 7 Troubleshooting
Table 7-1 Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Possible cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Whining noise that rises with speed | Low oil level or worn gear teeth | Top up the oil; inspect the gears if the noise stays |
| Knocking noise once per revolution | Damaged gear tooth | Stop the gearbox and inspect the gears |
| Oil leaks at a shaft | Worn shaft seal or blocked breather | Clean the breather; replace the seal |
| Oil temperature above 90 °C | Overload, wrong oil or dirty cooling fins | Check the load and the oil; clean the fins |

Field service report SR-2026-1213
Engineer: Kwame Asante.
Date: December 13, 2026.
Complaint: a whining noise from the HG-400 gearbox that rose with speed.
Findings: the oil level was below the sight glass and the oil had darkened; the last oil change was 14 months earlier.
The first-stage gear teeth showed light pitting.
Work done: drained and flushed the gearbox, refilled it with 18 liters of ISO VG 220 oil and replaced a leaking output shaft seal.
Recommended an oil analysis every six months.
